$comment: LUMA's scripted responses. GDD targets 120; these are the navigational and structural ones, which are the answers that do not depend on career content being authored yet. The rest arrive with content/memories and content/projects. Every entry is written in LUMA's voice: it never oversells, and it never invents a fact about the developer.

intents.answer: I am what is left of the part of him that kept notes. I remember where things are. I do not always remember why.
A portfolio, built as a world. Everything in it is also written down, plainly, in the Codex — you never have to play to read it.
W, A, S and D carry you. Hold shift and you hurry. Q and E turn you, and E takes hold of whatever is close enough to name.
Then do not walk. Ask me to open the Codex and everything opens at once — all of it, with nothing held back and nothing asked in return.
Ten of them, and each one names what broke in it. The Studio holds the machines; the Codex holds the write-ups.
Every project here carries its own failure, written by him, on purpose. A portfolio where nothing ever went wrong is a portfolio you cannot check.
Not as a row of percentages. Three honest levels: what he leads, what he works in, and what he would rather someone better than him held.
On a rail of hanging journals in the Archive, one for every year he turned up. Three of them are sealed; those are the ones that cost something.
The Tower, at the top, on brass. Or the Codex, at the bottom, in text. Both reach the same person.
A hundred of them, scattered where they happened. Each one you find opens its page in the Codex, permanently.
Every way out of a place stands on its edge, lit if it is open and grey if it is not. The grey ones say what they are waiting for.
Two things open doors here: how much of him you have remembered, and how many Fragments you carry. Nothing else, and no keys to fetch.
Eight. One waits at the end of each of the buildings that mattered. The Tower will not open for seven.
Ask a puzzle for a hint and it will give you one, then another, then the answer. Wait three minutes and it will offer to solve itself and still pay you.
Everything you do is kept the moment you look away. Come back on this machine and you will be standing where you left.
There is a cat. It is off the path, in the Forest. It does nothing at all, and it is the thing people remember.
Because a list of jobs tells you what someone did, and a world tells you how they think. The list is here too. He did not make you choose.
You are doing it now. Every memory you take back warms a little of this. At the fountain you can watch the number rise.
All of it can be walked from a keyboard, and all of it can be read without walking. The Codex is the whole of me, in text.
He did, in the evenings, over months. The Codex has his name, his history and his email. I only have his notes.
Right now, no. What you are hearing is written down in advance, by him, and I will not pretend otherwise.
Twenty minutes to see it. An hour or two to finish it. Ninety seconds if you take the Codex, and that is a real answer, not a lesser one.
